American Express reported higher third quarter 2026 net income of US$3,712 million and raised full year earnings guidance while keeping revenue growth expectations unchanged.

Fresh card partnerships with Airbnb and Albertsons expand American Express's travel and everyday spending reach, deepening its fee and rewards ecosystem across both premium and mass market customers.

The focus now turns to how American Express's stronger earnings guidance and ecosystem expansion might influence its longer term investment narrative.

See how American Express compares with other card networks and lenders by focusing on resilient balance sheets and fundamentals in our curated list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (25 results)

American Express Investment Narrative Recap

To own American Express, you need to be comfortable with a model that leans hard into premium customers, rich rewards, and high marketing and engagement spend against a high debt load. The raised 2026 EPS guidance and strong recent earnings keep that narrative intact. The key shorter term swing factor remains whether spending volumes and fee income can keep pace with those customer engagement costs.

The biggest operational risk still sits in rewards and co brand transitions. Variable customer engagement expenses already run at about 44% to 45% of revenue and portfolio sales are expected to weigh on billed business and net interest income through late 2026. The recent quarter and guidance update do not remove that pressure but they help reduce near term concern around it.

The most relevant fresh development for this story is American Express tapping bond markets with several new callable, senior unsecured variable rate notes totalling US$3.0b that mature in 2030 and 2034. This matters because the group already carries a high level of debt and relies entirely on higher risk wholesale funding rather than lower cost customer deposits.

For you as an investor, these offerings shape how the company funds ongoing card growth, marketing, and technology spend, and how interest expense trends against net interest income. Execution now is about keeping returns high while managing refinancing and rate risk on that wholesale funding stack. Any slip there would quickly feed back into the margin and earnings narrative investors are focused on.

What The Current Analyst Scenario Implies For American Express

American Express' narrative projects US$98.3b revenue and US$15.4b earnings by 2029. This rests on analysts assuming 11.5% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$4.1b from US$11.3b today.

title: Airbnb owners hit by £800m tax raid
detail:
Airbnb owners hit by £800m tax raid
Jonathan Prynn
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 8:54 AM CDT 3 min read
ABNB
Trade Airbnb on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
An estimated 450,000 Airbnb properties in Britain are available for short-term lets - iStock

Hundreds of thousands of Airbnb owners will be hit by John Healey's Budget tax raid on landlords, piling yet more pressure on Britain's tourism industry.

Treasury sources confirmed that short-term holiday lets will be hit by the 4pc additional tax on property income, as well as landlords renting out houses and flats for tenants to live in.

The surprise raid on the rental sector was one of a series of Budget tax grabs announced by the Chancellor on Wednesday, which will be used to fund headline giveaways such as the £100 energy bills handout to households.

Basic-rate income taxpayers will see the tax rate on property income rise from 20pc to 24pc from next April. Those in higher tax bands will see the rates on rental income rise to 44pc and 49pc.

Rachel Reeves had already signalled a 2p increase in her Budget last November, but Mr Healey went further in his Commons statement on Wednesday.

Industry leaders said the extra tax would be another significant blow for a sector still reeling from the prospect of a "holiday tax" on overnight stays from 2028.

Alistair Handyside, of the Professional Association of Self-Caterers, said: "It is incredibly unhelpful at a time when tourism is under so much pressure; it's yet another payment to find.

"A lot of people are going to say, 'I've done the maths, it's just not worth it any more.' It's not any individual straw that breaks people; it's the cumulative impact.

"All the costs are going up and now the Government is taking more, and of course we're not able to put up prices, so everyone's margin decreases again. They can't keep doing that; it just doesn't work."

OBR estimates suggest the new higher rates of property income tax will raise around £1bn in the 2028‐29 tax year before settling at around £800m in later years.

Pavan Mandir, at advisers UK Landlord Tax, said an Airbnb owner in the higher-rate tax band making a typical £24,000 profit will see their tax bill rise by £960 from £9,600 to £10,560.

An estimated 450,000 Airbnb properties in Britain are available for short-term lets.

Alongside rival online platforms such as Airbnb, Booking.com and Expedia-owned Vrbo hosted more than 100 million stays last year.

Many are owned by businesses or do not yet earn enough to pay income tax, leaving around 130,000 individuals declaring a total of £2.5bn in profits from holiday lets last year, according to HMRC.

Short-term holiday lets had not been classified as property businesses until April last year when a more generous tax treatment under the furnished holiday lettings regime was abolished.

Mr Mandir said: "Since the furnished holiday lettings regime was abolished from April 6 2025, holiday lets and Airbnb-style lets have formed part of your ordinary property business.

"That means there is no separate treatment for short-term lets."

Airbnb declined to comment.

title: What Does Booking Holdings Offer That Expedia Does Not?
detail:
What Does Booking Holdings Offer That Expedia Does Not?

Investors buy Expedia (EXPE) and Booking Holdings (BKNG) for the same thing: the hotel nights travelers book through them. Yet over the past year, Expedia stock returned 26.4% while Booking lost 25.9%. The two companies diverge on who brings in those bookings. Expedia credited B2B, its business supplying travel to partner companies, for its second-quarter revenue growth. Booking, meanwhile, builds on travelers who come straight to Booking.com. Booking said the direct share of its consumer business has held in the mid-60% range over the past four quarters. So what sets Booking apart from Expedia, and what did each company forecast for the rest of 2026?

Expedia Raised Its Forecast, Booking Holdings Lowered Its Own

In its August 5 report, Expedia raised its forecasts for 2026. A day earlier, Booking said it now expects lower gross bookings than it did before.

In the second quarter, Expedia's revenue rose 14.0% from a year earlier. Citing the strength of the first half, management raised its full-year revenue forecast to $16.1 billion at the midpoint, from $15.8 billion.

Booking posted an 8.1% revenue increase in the same quarter. Management said the lower bookings forecast came mainly from slower growth in flight tickets, and that its outlook for accommodation remained largely unchanged.

For you, those are different kinds of news. Expedia raised its revenue forecast for the business as a whole, while Booking's cut is about one part of its business. Expedia also lifted its full-year gross bookings forecast to $130 billion at the midpoint, from $128 billion. That is the measure Booking lowered. Both companies still expect slower growth in the third quarter, with Expedia guiding to revenue growth of about 5% to 8% and Booking to 4% to 6%.

Expedia Invests In Partners, Booking Hands Cash To Shareholders

Expedia is putting money into its partner business, while Booking is handing more of its cash back to shareholders. Expedia has over 70,000 partners, and in May, it announced its intent to acquire CarTrawler, a B2B car rental and insurance platform. On the August 5 call, management said partner mix and the pace of its own investment are the big drivers of B2B margins in the near term.

Expedia makes that investment while holding more cash than it owes. At the end of June, its cash and short-term investments exceeded its debt by $1.44 billion.

Booking's debt, by contrast, was $3.48 billion higher than its cash and short-term investments on the same date. Over the past twelve months, Booking's buybacks came to 9.1% of its market value, against 5.6% for Expedia. In the second quarter, Booking also raised new debt.

title: Should You Buy Booking Holdings Stock For Its Cash?
detail:
Should You Buy Booking Holdings Stock For Its Cash?
Trefis Team

Booking Holdings (BKNG) generates free cash flow equal to 8.3% of its market value, compared with 4.2% for the median S&P 500 company. A yield that high means either a business on sale or one the market expects to shrink, and Booking stock lost 25.9% over the past year as the S&P 500 gained 13.3%. So what does a cash yield like that give you as an owner?

What Booking's Cash Yield Gives You As An Owner

You own a portion of every dollar of that cash, just as you own a share of the profit, regardless of whether Booking pays it out or keeps it. Share prices tend to follow once the market recognizes the cash, and even more so when that cash is growing. That makes a high cash yield attractive: for each dollar you pay, you own more cash.

How Booking Makes So Much Cash

Booking earns money when travelers book room nights, flight tickets and attraction tickets through the platform. The company turned 33.8% of its revenue into free cash flow over the twelve months to June 2026. It needs little spending to keep running, with capital spending taking just 3.2% of the cash brought in by operations.

At Booking, the operating margin was 34.5% over those twelve months, compared with 18.5% for the S&P 500 as a whole. The margin widened from 32.8% a year earlier, and sales are still climbing, with revenue up 12.9% over the year.

Booking generated $9.54 billion in free cash flow in the twelve months to June 2026, up from $9.24 billion a year earlier. That rise of about 3% is far slower than the 12.9% growth in revenue. Free cash flow came to $7.51 billion in the twelve months to June 2024, and it has remained above zero in every twelve-month period ending between June 2023 and June 2026.

Cash largely offsets the company's debt. Booking owed $20.7 billion at the end of June 2026, compared with $17.2 billion in cash and short-term investments. Net debt, the gap between the two, comes to just 3.0% of Booking's market value. In the year to June 2026, its operating income was 8.8 times its interest expense.

Where Booking's Growth Is Slowing

Booking's own forecast points to slower growth, not a shrinking business. Management guided for revenue growth of 4% to 6% in fiscal Q3 2026, compared with the 8.1% Booking reported for fiscal Q2 2026.

On the August 4, 2026, call, management said elevated airline prices and reduced capacity due to the conflict in the Middle East pressured long-haul international travel, and that its guidance assumes those effects will persist through the third quarter. Management also said the expectation for gross bookings is lower than before, mainly because of lower flight ticket growth, while the outlook for accommodation remains largely unchanged. Management added that changes in Google's search display put some pressure on traffic driven by search engine optimization (SEO), which it called a small part of Booking's room nights.

Wall Street expects a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 5, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This company is expected to post quarterly earnings of $2.89 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +30.8%.

Revenues are expected to be $4.75 billion, up 16% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.05% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for ABNB
Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.
